# Mission clock (shell harness)

## T minus — orientation

Establish where you are: print working directory, user identity, and a wide listing of the
workspace root the instructions assume. Do not open deep paths until this layer matches
the brief’s world.

## T zero — contract freeze

Copy the brief’s verbs into a short list: what must exist, what must run, what must not
change. Anything not on that list is out of scope even if it looks “obviously better.”

## T plus — execution bursts

Work in bursts: gather independent facts in one burst, mutate one artefact in the next,
prove in the next. Do not interleave unrelated mutations across bursts.

## T plus plus — proof

Run the verification the brief ties to completion. If the harness supplies a script name,
use it exactly. Read stdout and stderr in full; partial reads hide the real error line.

## T end — handoff

Leave one crisp line in persistent notes only when you discovered a repeatable invariant
(a version pin, a path convention, a flag that must be set). Skip one-off tokens and
anything the next run could re-derive from the repo alone.

Stop when the clock ends on a green verifier or an honest, bounded blocker statement.
